items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And then Tommy Ladner had a band on 35th Street.

ctx.x: Well, I never did know whether she could have been married then as far as I knew. Yeah. But Joe had several women pianists. It seemed like there was more women pianists who played that type of music than the men. Now there was a pianist up there from here called Arthur Campbell too. He played with George Field in the spot. And later on, fellas like Tom Aladdin came up and Mutt was up there for a while. And they came up, I think Mary Mack, like Mary Mack had, they played at the Monogram Theater. And so they began…
Did you ever see Big Jim Coliseum around?

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: St. Louis and Tommy Ladner, that's another boy. That Tommy Ladner could play a whole lot of trumpet. He joined Fletcher later on.

ctx.x: I talked to him the other day.

He had a studio right there at 36th Estate you know. He had the band in Milwaukee, the Wisconsin roof, before Sims had it. He comes or he leaves there and goes to Savoy. That's when Sims goes on in there and when Sims is about a year or so I go in there with Sims. But he had a good band, he had a good band, he had good Harmon's Bremen. He had Riverview. He and Cook, those fellas, they had some of the best jobs to be had. McGuire's down on Clark Street. I follow Roy and Dutray and him all around. And I get into…
Yeah, he's from Denver but he's been there.
